:::{#exr-best-step-length}

#### The best step length for eigenvalues 1 and 9

[Gradient descent](optimization.qmd#def-gradient-descent) with a fixed step length <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
converges slowly if the step is too short and diverges if it is too long. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
@thm-best-constant-step gives the step length that shrinks the error bound fastest, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
from the smallest and largest [eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvalue) of $\matr{S}$.

Let $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 }$,
a [diagonal matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-diagonal-matrix), so its eigenvalues are its diagonal entries, 1 and 9. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
Using @thm-best-constant-step, find $\steplen^*$.

:::
